result.topic_en: Short mathematical exercises dated August 1796: an elementary proof of a product formula for cosines of multiples of π/13, a geometric proof that the cosines of the n-th roots of unity sum to zero, and a method for summing periodic series whose period sums to zero.
result.transcription:
Exercitationes Mathematicae.
Demonstratio elementaris propositionis de productis e Cosinibus.
$\sin\frac{1}{13}\pi\cdot\cos\frac{1}{13}\pi = \frac{1}{2}\sin\frac{2}{13}\pi$
$\frac{1}{2}\sin\frac{2}{13}\pi\cdot\cos\frac{2}{13}\pi = \frac{1}{4}\sin\frac{4}{13}\pi$ & sic porro
et si tandem $\sin\frac{2^n\pi}{13} = \pm\sin\frac{1}{13}$ erit
$\frac{1}{2^n} = \pm\cos.\frac{1}{13}\pi\cdot\cos.\frac{2}{13}\pi\cdot\cos.\frac{4}{13}\pi \ldots \cos\frac{2^{n-1}}{13}\pi$
Eodem modo demonstratur productum
$\cos\frac{m}{13}\pi\cdot\cos\frac{2m}{13}\pi \ldots \cos\frac{2^{n-1}m}{13}\pi$ dare idem productum
Hae veritates etiam aeque facile absque omni calculo
per solam polygoni inspectionem demonstrantur. Aug. 21. 96.

Perfacilis est demonstratio geometrica propositionis:
$\cos.0 + \cos\frac{2\pi}{n} + \cos\frac{4\pi}{n} + \cos 3\frac{2\pi}{n} \ldots \cos(n-1)\frac{2\pi}{n}$ esse $=0$
si polygonum in hoc situ consideretur: [figure]
Eodem.

Summa Serierum periodos quarum summa $=0$ tenentium commode invenitur si singula membra per successivas
variabilis cuiusdam $x$ potestates multiplicentur, unde
huius seriei [-...-] quae est recurrens summa sic exhibetur,
$\frac{a+bx+cxx\ldots}{1-x^n}$ quae pro nostro casu $x=1$ abit in
hanc formam $\frac{0}{0}$. Si valor huius expressionis per regulas notas
investigetur ad eadem pervenietur quae D. D. Bern. ex principio
metaphysico, sc. rationis sufficientis eruerat. Aug. 28. 96

methods.what: Repeated use of the double-angle formula sin x cos x = ½ sin 2x
Product of cosines of doubled angles equals ±1/2^n when 2^n π/13 returns to ±π/13 in sine
Same product holds for angles multiplied by m
Sum of cosines of the angles of a regular n-gon (roots of unity) is zero, proved geometrically
Summing a periodic series with zero period-sum via generating function (a+bx+cx²...)/(1-x^n) and evaluating the 0/0 limit at x=1
methods.quote:
$\frac{a+bx+cxx\ldots}{1-x^n}$ quae pro nostro casu $x=1$ abit in
hanc formam $\frac{0}{0}$

items.english: These truths can also be proved equally easily without any calculation, merely by inspecting the polygon.

investigetur ad eadem pervenietur quae D. D. Bern. ex principio

items.english: If the value of this expression is investigated by the known rules, one arrives at the same result that Daniel Bernoulli had derived from a metaphysical principle, namely that of sufficient reason.
